title: Significance of Influent C/N Ratios in Mainstream Anammox Process: Nitrogen Removal and Microbial Dynamics
content: Achieving simultaneous anammox and denitrification is a promising strategy to enhance nitrogen removal in mainstream anammox processes. However, the optimal influent C/N ratio and the microbial dynamics driving this process are still not fully understood. In this study, three mainstream anammox reactors were operated with varying influent C/N ratios. The results demonstrated a remarkable nitrogen removal efficiency of 92.6% achieved by combining partial denitrification and anammox, with the C/N ratio set at 1.0. Whereas, the nitrogen removal efficiency decreased when the C/N ratio was either 0.5 or 2.0, causing the accumulation of nitrate and ammonium in the effluent, respectively. These results suggest a narrow optimal range of the influent C/N ratio for mainstream anammox processes. Additionally, a transition in the predominant denitrifier population from Denitratisoma to Thauera was noted with the rise of the C/N ratio. The denitrifying phenotype of Thauera greatly depended on the C/N ratio. Only at a suitable C/N ratio, Thauera can effectively collaborate with anammox bacteria, partially reducing the nitrate generated in the anammox reaction. When the C/N ratio was high, Thauera primarily performed nitrite reduction, notably inhibiting anammox activity. The results of this study are valuable for the optimal design of the mainstream anammox process. In this study, the effects of carbon/nitrogen (C/N) ratio on mainstream anammox reactor were investigated.
